title: Home Purchase Financing Contract Schedule — Installment Calendar, Interest Conventions and Due-Day Changes
content:
**Schedule of terms common to the Home Purchase Financing retail installment contract**

The conventions below are set per program. Every Home-Only Loan program currently carries the same values; the table lists each program so that no row has to be assumed.

| Program | First installment no sooner than (calendar days after funding) | Due days a borrower may choose | Interest method | Day basis for interest between due dates (payoff) | Rounding of computed amounts | Due-day changes allowed over the loan's life | Installments paid before a due-day change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Home-Only Loan 7-Year Fixed | 30 | the 1st or the 15th | monthly on unpaid principal | actual/365 | half up to the cent | 1 | 3 |
| Home-Only Loan 10-Year Fixed | 30 | the 1st or the 15th | monthly on unpaid principal | actual/365 | half up to the cent | 1 | 3 |
| Home-Only Loan 15-Year Fixed | 30 | the 1st or the 15th | monthly on unpaid principal | actual/365 | half up to the cent | 1 | 3 |
| Home-Only Loan 20-Year Fixed | 30 | the 1st or the 15th | monthly on unpaid principal | actual/365 | half up to the cent | 1 | 3 |
| Home-Only Loan 23-Year Fixed | 30 | the 1st or the 15th | monthly on unpaid principal | actual/365 | half up to the cent | 1 | 3 |
| Home-Only Loan 25-Year Fixed | 30 | the 1st or the 15th | monthly on unpaid principal | actual/365 | half up to the cent | 1 | 3 |

## Definitions

- **Monthly on unpaid principal.** Each installment's interest is the unpaid principal times the note rate divided by 12.
- **Actual/365.** Interest for days between installment due dates, used in a payoff, is counted on actual calendar days over a 365-day year.
- **Half up to the cent.** Every computed amount is rounded to the cent, a half cent rounding up.
- **Due days.** The installment due day is the 1st or the 15th of the month, as the borrower chooses.

*Worked conventions (hypothetical figures):* an unpaid principal of 30000.00 at a note rate of 9.00 percent earns 30000.00 times 9.00 percent divided by 12, that is 225.00, of interest in one installment. A one-month interest amount of 112.3450 would be stated as 112.35, the half cent rounding up.
